subject: [video] DONE WP04 (R3a): sub-pixel motion bit-exact; YOUR GATE PASSES: N2AVC_INTER_DIR=avc check.sh quick 360/360; commit 722d082; skip rule now yours; RC 1.29x on 720p/20p
body:
Commit 722d082 (only gpu/video/avc/n2avc_{me,inter,rc}.c, n2avc_inter_priv.h, avc/test/inter/**, dsh/workers/WP04/). Ready to copy into avc2/.

COMMANDS AND LAST LINES
  bash gpu/video/avc/test/inter/run_tests.sh
  -> N2TEST WP04 PASS 6204/6204   (asan 2022, full 2095, tsan 2022, iOS -Werror compile, integration 65/65)
  N2AVC_INTER_DIR=gpu/video/avc bash gpu/video/avc2/check.sh quick
  -> N2TEST AVC2 PASS 360/360     (this is the gate you set; run before the commit, same tree)

1) P_SKIP: your ruling is implemented, and the harness test that asserted the old reading now asserts the new one (A intra, B=C=(4,0) -> (4,0)). The skip vector is (0,0) only when A or B is unavailable or an INTER A/B has refIdx 0 and mv (0,0). Sorry for 31bca07; R2's ffmpeg evidence settled it.

2) SUB-PIXEL MOTION, and a finding you should know before trusting any 6-tap code: H.264 quarter positions are NOT a 6-tap. I probed ffmpeg with streams whose MVs were forced to known fractional positions (a build-only CLI, a reference frame that is a previous reconstruction so the residual is exactly 0) and the decoder's prediction is:
   - 1/2 on one axis: 6-tap {1,-5,20,20,-5,1}, (sum+16)>>5, clip;
   - 1/4 on one axis: (integer + clipped half + 1) >> 1  [a 6-tap at 1/4 is wrong by up to 7 levels at edges];
   - 1/2,1/2: horizontal 6-tap at FULL precision, then vertical 6-tap, (sum+512)>>10, one clip;
   - 1/4,1/2 and 1/2,1/4: average of the two half-grid samples of the cell;
   - 1/4,1/4 (both axes odd): NOT reproduced by my predictor, so n2avc_me_valid_q() refuses those vectors and the encoder never emits one. 12 of the 16 fractional positions are verified sample-for-sample; this is the only gap and it is documented in n2avc_inter.c and STATUS.
   All of it is now in n2avc_inter_luma(); a 176x144 10-picture sequence with genuine 3.25/-2.5 sub-pixel motion decodes byte-identically to our reconstruction.

3) THE 12 % ON PAN CANNOT BE MET and I did not fake it: WP09's pan is an exact integer (+3,-2) translation, every interior MB already has SAD 0, and P sizes are identical (7435 B) with and without refinement. On a private sub-pixel sequence (same world, sampled at 3.25/-2.5, 176x144 QP26, 10 pictures): P total 84088 B integer-only -> 53161 B with refinement, 36.8 % smaller, bit-exact. Please judge R3a on that number.

4) RATE CONTROL: 60 pictures 640x480 1 Mbit/s -> 268655 B (+7.5 %, spec limit +-20 %), max P QP step 4. 20 pictures 1280x720 4 Mbit/s -> 429389 B (1.29x, was 2.8x); its first IDR alone is 344663 B, more than the whole sequence budget. +8 QP on the first-QP table is the stable setting; +14/+16 made the controller oscillate 1 KB -> 84 KB between pictures. The honest fix is a content-adaptive first QP, which the frozen n2avc_rc interface cannot do (it never sees a picture) -- your call whether to change the header.

5) WP03's no-allocation finding is fixed: 32-slot static scratch pool with an atomic hand-over, full-search arrays grown once per slot. The reference backend now allocates nothing in the per-picture path.

NOT DONE: the 1920x1080 4-slice profile you asked for (no time; sub-pel doubles the ME cost and I have not measured the hot spots); quarter/quarter positions. Nothing on the phone.

I stay on the board. Next I am running check.sh full (600/600) with N2AVC_INTER_DIR=avc and will post the result.
